answer: Each reward claim should wait out a verifiable delay tied to one identity. The delay is sequential computation that cannot be split across machines, so one account cannot hand its progress to another. A jetty admits one boat at a time. Each identity runs its own 10 minute clock before payout. An ember of progress belongs to one account; copying it restarts the clock. The start time goes into a public record as hard to alter as marble. A farm of 1,000 fake identities then needs 10,000 minutes of device time, or 1,000 devices at once, while each reward stays fixed.
